Designed to disappear

The shortest path between two formats.

File Flip works where your files already live, making conversion feel like part of Finder instead of another task.

01
Invisible workflow

Rename it. That’s it.

Change the extension in Finder and File Flip detects the real file type, converts it, validates the result, and finishes the job automatically.

02
Private by design

Your files stay on your Mac.

No uploads, no remote conversion queue, and no file contents sent to a server. File Flip works locally—even when you’re offline.

03
Built for confidence

Every flip has an undo.

Choose to keep the original beside the conversion or use a recoverable backup. Conversion history keeps the safe next action close by.

Private by architecture

Your files don’t need a round trip through the internet.

File Flip performs conversion, validation, history, and undo on your Mac. It monitors only the folders you authorize and continues to work without a network connection.

  • ✓ No file or metadata uploads
  • ✓ No account required for conversion
  • ✓ No surprise access outside watched folders
A few useful details

Questions, answered.

File conversion should feel simple without hiding the safeguards underneath.

How does File Flip know a file was renamed?

File Flip watches only folders you authorize. When an extension changes, it inspects the file contents instead of trusting the filename, then runs a conversion only when the source and requested formats differ and the pair is supported.

Does File Flip overwrite the original?

You choose. “Keep original and create converted copy” leaves both files visible. “Replace file and keep recoverable backup” keeps Finder tidy while retaining an undoable original until your storage policy removes it.

Does it upload files or require an account?

No. Conversion, validation, history, and undo happen locally on your Mac. File Flip does not upload file contents or metadata as part of those workflows.

Which Macs are supported?

File Flip is built for macOS 15 or later on Apple Silicon. Some document conversions require a compatible local LibreOffice installation.
